brief: A three-storey tower: drawers on the bottom storey and open bins on the top storey.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

5 drawers at level 0: drawer:0#0,0#cut on piece:0,0,0;half-n, drawer:0#-2,0#cut on piece:-2,0,0;half-s, drawer:0#-2,1#cut on piece:-2,1,0;half-s, drawer:0#-1,-1#cut on piece:-1,-1,0;half-s, drawer:0#0,-1#cut on piece:0,-1,0;half-s - all at level 0.

requirements.requirement: Open bins on the top storey (level 2)
requirements.evidence: 2 open bins at top storey level 2: bin:-1,0,2~hex-bin-full on piece:-1,0,2;full and bin:-1,1,2~hex-bin-full on piece:-1,1,2;full - both hex-bin-full are open bins.

finish.summary: Three-storey tower built from q=-1,r=0/1 columns levels 0-2 (249mm tall). Bottom storey carries 5 drawers on half-base cut faces; top storey (level 2) carries 2 open full bins. Mesh clear, check_build ok (LOOSE_BODY warning only informational).

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
